part.text:
All tests in the tree ran (66 total). The fix is complete and validated:

**Changes:**
- `lib/adapters/http.js:195-201` — the axios `maxBodyLength` default of `-1` (unlimited) is now always forwarded to the transport, mapped to `Infinity`. Previously, `-1` was silently omitted, letting `follow-redirects` apply its own hidden 10MB default — but only when `maxRedirects > 0` (with `maxRedirects: 0`, the plain `http` module was used and had no limit), which was the inconsistent behavior from the issue. Now the limit is uniform regardless of `maxRedirects`, and explicit `-1` (as well as `Infinity`) means unlimited.
- `README.md` — documented the default (`-1`, no limit).

**Test results:**
- The previously failing `should properly support default max body length (follow-redirects as well)` test now passes (a 20MB body succeeds with default config through `follow-redirects`).
- The 3 remaining failures (`max content length`, `HTTPS protocol`, `fromDataURI` Blob) were verified via `git stash` to fail identically on the unmodified baseline — they're pre-existing environment issues (network/SSL/Node version), unrelated to this fix.
